newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe said to drop French regional election reform.
newsitem.headline: Juppe said to drop French regional election reform.

text.p: Prime Minister Alain Juppe has decided to drop plans to reform the strict proportional representation voting system used for France's regional elections, a parliamentary aide said on Wednesday.

Michel Pericard, floor leader of the Gaullist RPR party, said after a coalition lunch at the prime minister's office he believed Juppe had given up on introducing a system to make it easier to find stable majorities in the 22 regional assemblies.
Asked to comment, Juppe said: "Mr Pericard's words are golden. We will see when the time comes."

Juppe had written to political party leaders earlier this year seeking their ideas on reforming several aspects of France's electoral system, including the regional elections. The next regional polls are due in 1998.

Proportional representation gave anti-immigration crusader Jean-Marie Le Pen's extreme-right National Front the balance of power in some regions in the last regional elections in 1992, forcing centre-right or left-wing coalitions to run minority executives with problems adopting a budget.

Maintaining the system could be seen as a favour to the National Front, which has failed to win any seats in the National Assembly due to the twin-ballot majority voting system even though it has about 15 percent national support.

"The prime minister thinks the status quo is the most desirable solution today...For the moment, he thinks there is nothing to change in the regional voting system," centre-right UDF party floor leader Gilles de Robien said.
